intro_text: Welcome. You are about to use a short demo of an ad-supported streaming service. Browse the catalogue and pick something to watch. The clip will play with one or two short ads, just like a real streaming service. Please keep this tab focused.

_notes.video_sources: All titles use publicly available CDNs. video_url is the primary; fallback_urls is tried in order if the primary fails. Sources: Google sample-videos bucket, Internet Archive (public-domain feature films), test-videos.co.uk (short H.264 demos), MDN shared-assets (CC0).
_notes.posters: Posters use Internet Archive thumbnail service or Google sample-images bucket; tile gradients fall back if a poster 404s.

_conditions_notes: Each session is assigned one of five ad conditions (A0–A4) per the pre-registered protocol. `condition_assignment_mode` controls how conditions are picked: 'fixed' uses `active_condition` for every session (use for development); 'random' picks uniformly from `random_pool` on session start. The query parameter ?cond=A2 overrides for testing and is logged so the experimenter can spot accidental overrides. The chosen condition's `ads` array is exposed to the client at cfg.ads, and the player schedules each placement (preroll, midroll, postroll, overlay, user_initiated) declaratively. Mid-roll/overlay start times can use `start_at_frac` (fraction of content duration, 0.0–1.0) and `start_at_cap_sec` (absolute cap so very long clips still get a mid-roll relatively early); the smaller resolved value wins. `duration_target_sec` hard-caps an ad's playback length so the 30-second spec is enforced regardless of the underlying asset length.

A0.label: Post-roll (control)
A0.description: A 30-second non-skippable ad plays after the clip ends, without interrupting playback. Baseline for both interruption-cost and agency-benefit comparisons.

A1.label: Forced pre-roll
A1.description: A 30-second non-skippable ad plays before the video begins. Playback is blocked until the ad completes. Goal interruption is shallow — the viewer has not yet initiated the content-consumption goal.

A2.label: Forced mid-roll
A2.description: A 30-second non-skippable ad interrupts playback at the midpoint of the clip. Goal interruption is deep — the viewer's ongoing narrative comprehension is halted at peak engagement.

A3.label: Non-interruptive overlay
A3.description: A semi-transparent banner occupies the lower-third of the frame for 30 seconds during playback; the clip continues uninterrupted. Presence is confirmed by a post-exposure item; non-noticers form a pre-registered subgroup.

A4.label: User-initiated
A4.description: Content plays normally; a persistent button visible from the start lets the viewer voluntarily watch a 30-second ad at any point. No bonus or reward is offered. The ad plays only if the viewer clicks. Non-clickers are retained for stated-preference analysis.

conditions._exp2_notes: Experiment 2 — 3×2 between-subjects (Explanation type E0/E1/E2 × Placement P1/P2). P1=forced mid-roll (high intrusiveness); P2=user-initiated (low intrusiveness). Conditions B0–B5 replace the ad library reference with the same creative used in Exp 1; update library_ref to your actual 30-second consumer-electronics creative before running the main study. The 'banner' field carries the explanation text rendered as 'Why this ad?' below the ad during playback.

B0.label: Exp2: No explanation, Mid-roll
B0.description: Forced mid-roll, no ad explanation (E0×P1). Control cell for Experiment 2.

B1.label: Exp2: Content-based explanation, Mid-roll
B1.description: Forced mid-roll with content-based explanation (E1×P1). Banner reads 'Why this ad? This ad was selected based on what you watch on this platform.'

B2.description: Forced mid-roll with data-based explanation (E2×P1). Banner reads 'Why this ad? This ad was selected based on your browsing history and demographic profile.'
